issues.title: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany provides update on Lennart Karl’s health status
issues.summary: Another game, another injury scare, as Bayern Munich’s Lennart Karl was substituted early by Kompany to manage his load.
issues.content_html:
Bayern Munich is facing its worst ever injury crisis in recent memory.

All of Bayern Munich’s starters in attack are out with injuries, with left-winger Luis Diaz making his way back with scrimmage minutes. To add insult to injury, Bayern’s 18-year-old phenom Lennart Karl was subbed out early in the second half, causing fans to panic, and understandably. There is an impending sense of doom every time a player succumbs to injury or a health issue, with the squad struggling both domestically and in the Champions League.

During the postgame press conference (as captured by @iMiaSanMia), coach Vincent Kompany was asked about the status of Bayern star Lennart Karl. Kompany doused the flames with his response. “Lenny wasn’t injured. The plan was actually not to have Lenny play another full 90 minutes today. We mustn’t forget that the boy is only 18.”

Phew, at least that isn’t another injured player.

Bayern barely has a fieldable XI as is, and any more absences will mean more recruits from the youth reserves. At the moment, both the Bundesliga and the Champions League are salvageable. However, things could get really ugly for this paper-thin squad, with five games in just three weeks before the winter break, and a host of important fixtures ready to bludgeon the squad in January.

Just please do not lose to Manchester United.

issues.title: OTB Staff Picks 2026: Rutgers vs Michigan State
issues.summary: Will our staff get the score right for the final game of the season?
issues.content_html:
After defeating Penn State 25-24 in Happy Valley last week, Rutgers football will play its final game of the season at home this Saturday, 11/28 at 4:15 pm against Michigan State. The Scarlet Knights, 3-8, will face the 3-8 Spartans, who are coming into this game after losing to No. 13 Oregon 45-7. As is tradition here at OnTheBanks, the staff will try to guess the score of the game and give context as to why they think that way.

Andrew Rice

Well, folks, we made it to the end of what has been a wild ride of a season. Never did I think we would lose to UMass and beat Penn State in the same year, but here we are; such is the craziness and beauty of college football.

Michigan State will be short-handed at quarterback and will have to rely on freshman Kayd Coffman to lead the team after an ugly performance against Oregon. If the Scarlet Knights can even partially replicate their defensive performance against Penn State, it should be enough to provide the offense several opportunities to pull away.

The key offensively will be if Rutgers can find a way to run the ball against the Spartans’ stout defensive line. Ben Roberts and Eli Coenen anchor the defensive tackle position for Michigan State and could cause disruption if not handled properly. However, outside of these two, the Spartan defense seems to be below average, and with AJ Surace having his best passing game last game, things seem to be trending up for the Knights’ offense. Again, if they can find a way to at least partially replicate last week’s performance, it should provide the lift they need to win. With all of these factors seemingly going in the Knights’ favor, Rutgers will prevail in a close one.

Rutgers 24, Michigan State 21 Ryan Castellano

First and foremost, I would like to apologize to Greg Schiano for doubting how badly he wanted to beat Penn State. I would also extend this same apology to AJ Surace, for recommending that he shouldn’t have played due to his broken ribs. This was clearly the best game of the Schiano II era, and Surace’s best start in Scarlet.

I find it fitting that to kick off the holiday season, Rutgers was effectively given a gift by playing the worst team in the Big Ten to finish this season. Now for the bow on top. Michigan State comes to Piscataway fresh off a 45-7 loss at Oregon. Kayd Coffman makes his third career start at quarterback, and the Spartans’ injury report ran 16 names deep last week.

More importantly, it’s Senior Day. Rutgers has 48 seniors on the roster, and the class will be honored during the Scarlet Walk before kickoff. That group includes Clay Thevenin, who caught the two-point conversion that beat Penn State a week ago, Frenchtown’s own Logan Blake at tight end, and Dantae Chin, a Comeback Player of the Year watch list pick up front. It also includes two seniors who won’t get one last snap for this game: Kwabena Asamoah, the preseason All-American who anchored the offensive line, and Dylan Lonergan, who opened the season as the starting quarterback, are both done for the year. They’ve earned the walk as much as anyone else.

Greg Schiano said this week that for some of these guys, Saturday will be the last time they ever put a helmet on. After what this team did in Happy Valley, I don’t think they’ll let that last time be a loss, let alone a close game.

Rutgers 28, Michigan State 10

Arnav Sarkar

Rutgers fans, we were all so far off last week against Penn State, but coming off the stunning win in State College, there is a lot of room for optimism as the Scarlet Knights host Michigan State for their season finale. With both teams sitting at 3-8 records, this game will be a chance to avoid the bottom of the conference standings and build momentum into the offseason and into next season.

The Spartans are coming off a devastating 45-7 loss to a streaking #12 Oregon, but have pulled off their own upset victory with a 15-6 win over Michigan earlier this month. The game will likely come down to a few things, including the quarterback matchup. Freshman Kayd Coffman will be making his third start after losses to UCLA and the Ducks, while Rutgers will likely bring out AJ Surace after his heroic efforts to bring the Knights over the line against the Nittany Lions.

Rutgers will have to contend with Michigan State’s stout defensive line and ground game, including Iowa transfer Jaziun Patterson, who has taken lead back duties after the Spartans lost Cam Edwards earlier this season. But the Scarlet Knights’ defense stepped up, especially against the run, and on offense, Surace used his tight end, running backs, and wide receivers to move the ball and dissect Penn State’s defense.

This game could go one of two ways. Either Rutgers feeds off their momentum and pushes towards another win on Senior Day and in front of the home crowd, or last week’s miracle win took a significant toll on them and that affects their performance. My bet is on the Scarlet Knights. With Michigan State favored by around three points, Rutgers does not need a two-touchdown comeback as they hold off Sparty at home to end the season on a two-game conference win streak. How great would that feel after the way this season has gone?

Rutgers 20, Michigan State 14

Bob Cancro

Well, this is certainly a different prediction than it was going to be a week ago.

We all ate crow, we all tipped our hat to Greg Schiano & Co. They did a great job doing what none of us thought they could. The skill players played with skill. And, maybe most significantly, AJ Surace played inspired ball. He was Willis Reed returning from a torn thigh muscle to rally the 1970 Knicks to a title. He was Emmitt Smith with a separated shoulder to lead Dallas to the NFC East title in’93. He was Kirk Gibson pinch-hitting a walk off home run despite being hobbled. The kid is a gamer.

And as has been noted, the schedule could not be more helpful: at home, the bottom dwelling Spartans, Senior Day. The only concern I have is the crowd; Rutgers has never drawn well on Thanksgiving weekend. I hope people turn out.

To help Surace and to shorten the game, I think a heavy dose of Raymond/Thevinin should make this a Rutgers victory.

Pat Fitzgerald is a good coach; I like him and I think he’ll right the ship in East Lansing; it seems like Sparty wants to make that happen. But, Schiano can motivate kids; he’s shown that. I think that this game – for Rutgers – is like the SEC: it just means more.

Rutgers 27, Michigan State 17

issues.title: Remco Evenepoel reportedly considering Omloop Het Nieuwsblad debut to start 2027 season
issues.summary: Belgian media report that double Olympic champion could make his first appearance at the cobbled Classic on February 27
issues.author: Lyne Lamoureux
issues.content_html:
After finishing third at the Tour of Flanders back in April, Remco Evenepoel is reportedly considering starting his 2027 season on the cobbles at Omloop Het Nieuwsblad, according to Belgian media. It would mark his debut at the race in the heart of the Flemish Ardennes, which features many of the same cobbles and bergs as the Tour of Flanders.

According to Belgian newspaper La Dernière Heure, the Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe rider will tackle the opening race of the Spring Classics on February 27, 2027. That would set him up for the Tour of Flanders, five weeks later. They also report that Liège-Bastogne-Liège, where he finished third this year, still figures in his plans on April 25.

However, not all Belgian media agree, as HLN reports that a start at Omloop is not set yet, as there are other options on the table.

Last month, the double Olympic champion said that he wanted to start the season later than he did this year, when he made his debut with his new team, with wins in Mallorca in late January.

What about Paris-Roubaix? Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe CEO Ralph Denk is open to the Belgian making his debut at Hell of the North, but the decision has to come from Evenepoel himself, as he told Eurosport last month.

We won't have to wait long for more clarity, with Evenepoel's full schedule expected to be revealed in December.

After ending his season with a win at Chrono des Nations mid-October, Evenepoel has had a busy off-season. He travelled to Northern California for wind tunnel testing at Specialized at its Morgan Hill headquarters, and then took a side trip to Southern California to scout the courses for the 2028 LA Olympic Games. After some time off in Tokyo, Japan, Evenepoel is now back to training in Mallorca.

The 26-year-old is expected to return to the Tour de France in 2027 after finishing runner-up to Tadej Pogačar in July. The route could suit the Belgian, with 71km of individual time trials and relatively few brutal mountaintop finishes.

Evenepoel’s full schedule will be revealed at Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe's media day at their first training camp for 2027 on December 11.

We spotted this deal lurking on the Specialized Black Friday sales page, and we wanted to highlight it for you.

The Alpha Prime jacket is a lightweight, softshell jacket that's lined with Polartec Alpha insulation, which helps it breathe, adds lightweight insulation, and wicks moisture well.

It's a fantastic jacket to wear; it's super soft and comfortable and adds a nice amount of insulation. I'm lucky enough to own one, and love using it for steadier spins and as a top layer at events.

Worn over a base layer or jersey, it's perfect for cool winter or autumnal days, though it isn't waterproof so you'll want to put a hardshell over the top when the heavens open.

issues.title: Nate Bargatze Is (Sort Of) Leading By Example
issues.summary: One of the biggest comedians in the world, Nate Bargatze’s career path was anything but straightforward.
issues.author: Tyghe Trimble
issues.content_html:
It’s a bit hard to believe that Nate Bargatze, one of the biggest comedians today, met his wife while working at Applebee’s in Tennessee. Or that on his first job overseeing the dog kennel in an amusement park (apparently a thing), he let the dog out (“it was a whole thing … and that was kind of the end of the dog kennel”). Or even the basic fact that at the height of his career he decided to move back to Tennessee so that his teen daughter might have a more normal life. Bargatze’s life, like his comedic work, reads like a folksy tall tale. It draws you in with the details and lulls you with its sense of warmhearted authenticity — then lands a punchline.

But authenticity matters to him, in his storytelling and what he’s learned over the years. He recently brought some of his experience to Ford’s Accelerate conference, where he is a spokesperson for what they’re calling the “essential economy” — of skilled technicians and tradespersons, a group that, according to economists, is in short supply and needs to grow. Bargatze is an interesting choice for this forum, a comedian with a high school degree and no formal trade skills besides those he learned onstage. He went to community college for a year and worked a variety of jobs, from waiting at Applebee’s to reading water meters. But he gets the value and opportunity in trade school. “I relate to it very much, because I’m someone that should’ve went to these trade schools. I did not go to college ... They’re going to really learn something and have a craft and know how to do something that is going to be, I believe, important for just the future.”

He also is thinking about this because his 14-year-old is not too far from entering the workforce. “Right now it’s like, yeah, I don’t know if she’s wrapping her head around it. But then, as she continues to get older, she will wrap her head around it. She doesn’t have a sense of urgency of cleaning her room, so you work on that and you just keep saying it and you need to [instill that urgency] as a parent. And if you don’t, your kids watch you. So if you don’t have any kind of sense of urgency, they’re going to pick that up from you.” Which all boils down to a most authentic parenting philosophy: “Be a good example, basically.”

Tell me about what you’re doing right now at this Ford Accelerate event.

What Ford is doing with this event that we’re at right now, where they’re showing kids going into trade schools ... letting kids know that this is kind of the future, that they’re going to have jobs. And it’s like we don’t know where jobs are going with AI and all this stuff, but the trade schools… We need that. I relate to it very much, because I’m someone that should’ve went to these trade schools.

I worked the water meters. I did not go to college. They’re going to get more college than I did. But they’re going to really learn something and have a craft and know how to do something that is going to be, I believe, important for just the future. I think they’re putting themselves in such a great position, probably better than they realize now, but they’re going to, I think, look back and just be like, “Man, that was such a good call.”

I’m wondering, since we’re talking about work, what’s the most important thing you’ve learned about work in your life?

I always go back to when I waited tables at one point and our manager there always talked about a sense of urgency. And that’s always stuck with me for some reason. It was just going to a table and just have a sense of urgency. It goes a long way when you get to that table and they really feel like they’re being taken care of. I think I’ve just kept that even as I’ve gone forward. If you respond to emails or my team is talking to you, I don’t want to be like, “I’ll get to them next week.” You kind of want to just be like, “No, let’s get to them and let’s make sure that we stay on top of it.”

Speaking of people who don’t have it, how do you instill that sense of urgency in your kid without them fighting back?

You say stuff as a parent, you don’t know what’s sticking and what’s not sticking. You keep talking about it, and the older she gets — she’s 14 now — the more she’s going to see examples of it. Right now, I don’t know if she’s wrapping her head around it, but then as she continues to get older, she will wrap her head around it. She doesn’t have a sense of urgency of cleaning her room. So you work on that and you just keep saying it and you need to do it as a parent. And if you don’t do it, your kids watch you. So if you don’t have any kind of sense of urgency, they’re going to pick that up from you. And so, be a good example, basically.

Then what’s one thing you wish your kids had today that you had during your childhood?

I think not the internet, maybe. That would be something, even though it’s great and the connection and it’s all this stuff, you just wish they would’ve had a little more... I think innocence lasted longer when we grew up because you just weren’t pounded with information all day long.

What’s your wife love about you?

I hope me for being me. We’ve been together before any of this started. We met at Applebee’s. Our 20th wedding anniversary is Oct. 13. I think it’s taking time to get used to it, but we’re along this ride together and just the surprises. We don’t know where everything’s going to end up or what’s going to happen. I think that she sees that I work hard at stuff and has been behind the scenes and loved me before any of this and loves me now. So it’s just to have the support from her, I wouldn’t be here without her. And she very much kept me grounded in a world when you come up in comedy that you could not be... It’s easy to not be grounded.

On the flip side, what do they maybe find annoying about you?

She doesn’t like eating near me because she thinks I’d chew loud. I don’t think I’m too loud. I think it’s very normal. But she gets very uncomfortable if she’s like... I mean, if she’s on the couch and I’m at the table right behind the couch, she cannot stand it. So I eat outside now — and I only do soups.

What kind of dad are you? How would you describe yourself as a dad?

I like to be... You find moments to talk to your kid. As they get older, they have friends. She’s young and all that, so they want to run with their friends. A big part is finding the moments of when they can get very talkative, and so you can find these little pockets and really try to home in on those.

She knows I’m a fun time. She can take me for a ride, where her mom can put her foot down a little bit more. She knows where to go. She thinks very much like me, and she can work you if she wants something, and she works me quite a bit.

Coming back to the work thing, what was your first job?

My first job, I worked at Opryland Theme Park in Nashville. I was 15, and so I was a sweeper. I walked around and just swept up the park. And I also did the dog kennel. After the sweeper, I got promoted to dog kennel.

The dog kennel?

Well, because people would bring their pets because they’re on vacation and they’d travel with their pets.

Oh.

So you can’t bring them to the park. And so people would bring their dogs in or whatever, their cats. I think we had a chicken. People travel with some weird animals. But one dog got out, and so it was a whole thing. And that was kind of the end of the dog kennel. I think I went back to sweeping after that. But he got out, and so we had to call the... again, pre-internet, so you got to announce to the park, “Whose German shepherd got out in the parking lot?” And then they got to go search for this dog and it was under a parked car. And yeah, I still talk to that family today.

I’m sure you don’t. They don’t want to talk to you.

No. But I bet they still remember it. We both still remember that.

issues.title: Nick Viall Opens Up About Fatherhood
issues.summary: The former Bachelor star and now co-hose of Age of Attraction and The Viall Files co-host (with his wife, Natalie Joy Viall is now a dad of three — including infant twins. Here's how it's going.
issues.author: Tyghe Trimble
issues.content_html:
Nick Viall first appeared on “The Bachelorette” 12 years ago and ever since, he’s had one serious reality TV run. From “Bachelor in Paradise” to “Dancing With the Stars,” “The Masked Singer” to “Age of Attraction,” which he currently co-hosts with his wife, Natalie Joy Viall , his handsome mug is everywhere. He also notably doles out relationship advice, also alongside his wife, on the The Viall Files, one of the most popular relationship podcast on Apple that airs three to four times a week.

What viewers might not know is that this Wisconsinite, the second oldest of 11 siblings, has a two-year-old and, since July, twin infants. So how’s twin dad life? “When you tell people you're expecting ... people are more prone to just kind of, I call doomsday kind of advice,” he tells Fatherly. “And then it happens, and you're so happy and everything feels like a blessing.” We caught up to give Nick the Cool Dad questionnaire and it seems he didn’t want it to end. “It's fun to talk about fatherhood,” he says. Which is good, because he’s got a lot of fathering on his hands right now.

How's being a twin dad going? I have had friends who were twin parents, and it's so … much.

Overall, it's great. I mean, I think every stage is different. With newborns — it sounds like you're a father as well, so as you know — they're just little potatoes at first. And for the most part, other than the regular feedings and having to wake up multiple times in the middle of the night, which can get tiring, it's not too bad. But obviously those moments … pockets of overwhelmingness of like, "Oh, no." One cries, and then you calm one down, and then another one cries.

For the most part, I was joking with Natalie, my wife, about it honestly, because you get so nervous about twins. A lot of times when you tell people you're expecting ... People are more prone to just kind of give what I call doomsday advice where it's like, "Oh, get ready for hell," or something like that. And then it happens, and you're so happy and everything feels like a blessing For the most part, it just feels like you got a BOGO, like a buy one, get one free. And it's like, great. Obviously, my wife during the pregnancy, different experience. Obviously, I think it's a lot more on mothers to carry two than one.

But it's been really exciting to just be like, "Oh, we already have three kids, and it only took two pregnancies." So easy for me to say, obviously, but it's been really fun.

Well, congratulations. The first question I have is just wondering what kind of dad are you?

I'm a pretty involved dad and pretty hands-on. Natalie and I, ever since we've been together, we just share the responsibilities of our household. And that was true even before we became parents. I was lucky enough to have the parents I had. And I think that the biggest takeaway I had from my childhood is just how my parents worked as a team.

I have 10 brothers and sisters. And my parents were very lower middle class, very blue collar. My mom stayed home and worked. I mean, my mom stayed home and raised the kids, my dad worked, but that wasn't based on some kind of a decision they made. It was more like that was the situation they had.

In terms of the day-to-day, they shared their responsibility. My mom did a lot of the traditional day-to-day keeping up the house, but my dad would often make dinner. My mom sometimes would mow the lawn. It was just more like all hands on deck type of thing, and you just do things as a team. And that's just something Natalie and I implemented into our relationship early on. And then, obviously, when River showed up, it continued. And then Natalie started working with me on the show.

And so really we're just very involved. And so any little thing I can do to help Natalie or just be an involved parent, we're doing things together every step of the way.

So I'm just hyper-involved. There's no her thing, my thing. We conquer and divide, and certainly, we joke where I'm allergic to laundry, she's allergic to dishes. I don't mind doing dishes. She doesn't mind doing laundry. So there's definitely things that we have our preferences, but for the most part, we just share everything.

What's one thing you wish your kids had today from your childhood or will have?

Well, I feel very fortunate to say that I was lucky enough to try to be able to give the best part of my childhood to my children because I was lucky enough to buy back my grandfather's lake house a couple years ago. And that was a place that in my childhood was like my Nirvana. It was my special place.

Sadly, when my grandfather passed away when I was in the fourth grade, they sold that property, and it was like this devastating moment of my life. It was like some real childhood trauma.

And it was a place that, quite frankly, I had recurring dreams all the way into adulthood. And again, I was lucky enough to buy it back and just really excited that it will be a place that I'll hopefully be able to give to my children, and a place that they'll be able to grow up and we'll have, obviously, a lot of hopefully monumental family events there. So that's definitely something I want them to have.

But thinking in the vein of how times might be different, I think the world's changing so fast. I have such fond memories of going to the movies as a child, going to Blockbuster and picking on a movie and things like that. And some of those moments I hope we'll still be able to do. Or just maybe I hope there's a renaissance of people wanting to get outside, touch grass type of thing. And I hope that's something our children will be able to enjoy.

And certainly, in the lake houses up in the middle of nowhere in Wisconsin will be a great tool to help our kids want to be outside and play in nature and just make-believe. Most of my childhood was a lot of just make believe with my friends outside. And we would ride our bikes all over the place.

It's weird. I'm sure you're probably familiar with that book, The Anxious Generation by Jonathan … he talked about the freedoms that kids used to have back in the day and parents like 5, 10 years ago got a little... it's like you get nervous about the world, but you took for granted, again, the dangers of the phone. And so I'm really hoping my kids get to embrace the world and get outside and play make believe with their friends and things like that. So that's a big focus for us and certainly, hopefully, something that I hope they do get to enjoy because those are always fond memories that I have as a child.

That's a great perspective. I mean, I do agree that right now is a good time to have kids because everyone is much more aware of the difficulties parents are facing . You'll see all the support in elementary school. It's really talked about a lot.

And on to the next question: What does your wife love about you?

Well, I think probably just the fact that, I hope, that I like to think I'm her rock. There's so much burden and pressure on moms postpartum. I like to think that my job is just to be a cheerleader. When I get a sense that she's stressed out or feeling overwhelmed, I'm quick to try to give her a break, tell her to go lie down if that's what she wants to do. I'm always there and always available.

And I hope that's one thing that she loves most about me, but I just try to be as supportive as possible just to remind her and just be a cheerleader. Just always remind her that she's doing a great job because, again, there's just so much pressure that moms put on themselves.

The other side of that coin, what does she maybe find annoying about you?

Oh, my God, the list is so long. Well, I don't know how to close a cupboard. I don't put things away. I leave a trail of destruction wherever I go. I'm messier than our two-year-old. So there is that.

I've recently got back into some video game playing, which definitely gives her the ick, but she is kind enough to let me decompress with a game here or there. So I think she'd prefer it not to exist, but … everything in moderation. Again, the trick for any dad out there who enjoys a video game or two is to never let it get in the way of being helpful. So that's the trick to get it in when you can, but never let it come in the way of, obviously, being a partner and being a father.

What does fatherhood mean to you in the current world?

I mean, it means everything to me. I've had this conversation with a lot of peers that I have, and I have a lot of women friends in the space I work in, and so talked to some new young mothers, young professionals who, obviously, their careers are and still are really important to them.

Once you have a child, I describe it as the easiest North Star. I've been fortunate enough in my life to accomplish a lot of cool things and it's nice to have individual accomplishments and accolades and awards, but they're not always as fulfilling as you think they might be when they happen. Fatherhood, parenthood is just... you always know why you're doing something. You always know what the purpose is. And so even the late nights, it's a drag to get up at 2:00 in the morning, but you know why you're doing it, and you always get a sense of purpose and accomplishment. And it's just the best motivator. No matter what's going on in work or in our personal life, it really calms you down.

I'm a fairly anxious, high-stress guy. It's easy for me to get worried about work and all the things that are going on in this world. And then I have the benefit of coming home, and especially with River now when she greets me. I'm constantly on my phone with work, and I'm never not working in a sense, but when I walk into the house, Natalie's incorporated this kind of best practice of making sure I'm off my phone and I'm very present to greet River. Even if it's for a few minutes, even if I still have some work left to do, I never walk in on the phone and I'm not giving her my undivided attention. And it's something like Natalie incorporated, which I really appreciate that she did, and I think it's just a really great best practice that we do.

Thank you so much for all the thoughtful answers.

I appreciate it, man. It's fun to talk about fatherhood.

It truly is.

It's something I really enjoy. And it's weird because in my... I don't know if you've noticed this. I mean, it's weird how parenting has become, like everything else these days, almost like a polarizing topic. No parent is indifferent about parenting, and obviously, every parent comes with passion, but it's weirdly become a topic that I'd want to talk about more, but sometimes it's like you want to be careful because you don't want to force your thoughts and feelings onto others.

issues.title: Sneezing After You Put Up the Tree? You Might Have Christmas Tree Syndrome
issues.summary: Christmas tree syndrome can cause allergy-like symptoms during the holidays. Learn what triggers it and how to keep trees and decor clean. The post Sneezing After You Put Up the Tree? You Might Have Christmas Tree Syndrome appeared first on Family Handyman .
issues.author: Alex Shoemaker
issues.content_html:
Being at home during the holidays can be a magical time of year for many. But for some, it also means dealing with allergies. Christmas tree syndrome could be responsible. Sneezing might start soon after the Christmas decorations go up, sometimes happening around the same time every year.

Dr. Racheal Onah, ND, consulting physician with RealTime Labs, explains what causes it, which symptoms to watch for, and how families can reduce their exposure.

What Is Christmas Tree Syndrome? Causes, Symptoms, and Prevention

Christmas tree syndrome refers to allergy and asthma symptoms that appear after putting up a Christmas tree or holiday decorations. Onah explains that the term is a nickname, not an official diagnosis, though the reactions are real.

Real Christmas trees can bring mold, pollen, and other allergens into the house. A study published in the Annals of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology identified several types of mold on Christmas trees, including some that can cause allergies.

“Outdoors, molds play a part in nature by breaking down dead organic matter such as fallen leaves and dead trees, but indoors, mold growth should be avoided,” explains the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. “Molds reproduce by means of tiny spores; the spores are invisible to the naked eye and float through outdoor and indoor air.”

Symptoms can include, but are not limited to:

  • Wheezing or coughing
  • Itchy nose or watery eyes
  • Chest tightness, especially for people with asthma
  • Fatigue or trouble sleeping
  • Itchy skin or a rash on the hands and forearms

Symptoms that get worse around the tree but improve away from home may point to an allergy. Onah says frequent sneezing and itchy eyes without a fever suggest an allergic reaction rather than a virus. A cold is more likely to bring a fever, sore throat, or body aches.

Onah suggests checking for mold or musty smells before buying a real tree. She recommends having the tree lot shake off loose debris, then rinsing the tree outside and letting it dry before bringing it indoors. Once inside, Onah recommends keeping the tree away from heating vents and running a HEPA air purifier in the same room.

Can Artificial Christmas Trees Cause Christmas Tree Syndrome and Allergies?

Artificial trees can cause problems, too, depending on where and how they’re stored.

“Artificial trees that sat in a garage or basement for 11 months have had plenty of time to collect dust and moisture,” says Onah. “They are often stored in the original cardboard boxes they came in, which is a material that holds onto humidity and can feed mold on its own.”

Wreaths, garlands, and fabric decorations can collect dust or develop mold in storage as well. Scented candles and artificial snow sprays may also bother people with allergies.

Onah recommends unpacking decorations outside and wiping down artificial branches before setting them up. She says glass, metal, and hard plastic ornaments can be washed with warm water and mild dish soap. Porous decorations with visible mold or a musty smell, such as fabric, paper, or wood pieces, should be thrown away.

“When the season is over, make sure everything is completely dry before you pack it away,” says Onah. “Use sealed plastic bins instead of cardboard, add a few silica gel packets to absorb moisture, and store everything off the floor. If possible, opt to store your bins in a climate-controlled space like an interior closet rather than a garage, attic or basement.”

Anyone dealing with recurring allergy symptoms or worsening asthma should check with a healthcare provider.

“I’d pay extra attention if symptoms linger after the decorations come down,” says Onah. “This could be a sign the decor stirred up a bigger mold problem in the home, like a damp storage area or an HVAC system that’s harboring growth.”

Sources

  • Dr. Racheal Onah, ND, registered naturopathic doctor and consulting physician with RealTime Labs
  • Annals of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology, “Identification of mold on seasonal indoor coniferous trees”
  • U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, “A Brief Guide to Mold, Moisture and Your Home”
  • U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, “Mold”

The post Sneezing After You Put Up the Tree? You Might Have Christmas Tree Syndrome appeared first on Family Handyman.

issues.title: This DIY Coffee Station Can Be Built Using Only Scrap Wood
issues.summary: Clear the counter clutter and fuel your mornings with a scrap-wood coffee station that has a spot for everything. The post This DIY Coffee Station Can Be Built Using Only Scrap Wood appeared first on Family Handyman .
issues.author: Carmen De La Paz
issues.content_html:
Glue up the panels

Boards wide enough for the top (A) and base (B) are almost impossible to find, so I made the panels by joining several boards with biscuits.

Cut the boards at least 1/2-in. longer and wider than needed. The extra material lets you trim the panels square and to size after the glue dries.

Mark across each joint where you want a biscuit, spacing them 6- to 8-in. apart and about 3-in. from each end. Cut the slots with a biscuit joiner. Be generous with the glue in the slots and along the edges. You want an even bead of squeeze-out so you know you have good coverage. Clamp the panels and keep them flat as they dry.

Once the glue dries, scrape off the squeeze-out and cut the top (A) and base (B) to the final size. Then cut the rest of the parts following the cutting list.

Attach the back and sides

Connect the two sides (C) and the back (E) to the base (B) of the coffee organizer using 18-gauge brad nails and wood glue. Secure the sides so they’re flush with the bottom of the base. Set the back on the base between the sides, flush with the back edges of the base (B) and sides (C).

Make the butcher block

Cut the pieces for the butcher block (L) and biscuit-join them the same way you did the panels. Again, cut them at least 1/2-in. oversize. That allows for the wood shifting during clamping and leaves enough on each end to make clean, square cuts once the glue has dried.

Once the glue is dry, cut the butcher block to final size on the table saw. Scrape and sand off the dried glue, then round over the sharp edges with a router and a bearing-guided 1/4-in. round-over bit.

When you size the butcher block, leave room for the drawer slides you’ll install later. Most need about 1/2-in. on each side, so a 13-in. opening takes a 12-in.-wide butcher block.

Install the center divider

The left-hand compartment houses the butcher block and drawer, so it needs to be 13-in. wide: 12-in. for the butcher block and drawer, plus 1-in. for the drawer slides. Mark the divider location, then test-fit the butcher block and loose drawer slides to confirm the opening. Apply glue and secure the center divider (D) with 18-gauge brad nails driven up through the base (B) and in through the back (E).

Note: Drawer slide clearance varies by style and manufacturer. Check your slides’ specs and adjust the opening as needed.

Assemble the drawer

Build a drawer to store coffee pods and spoons. Glue and nail the drawer box front and back (G) to the ends of the sides (F), then attach the bottom (H) to square it up. The drawer front (K) covers the nails on the front.

Secure the drawer dividers (J) inside the drawer (Fig. B) with wood glue and brad nails, spacing them to fit your coffee pods, spoons, or other items. Feel free to add or take away dividers as needed. I left 1-1/2-in.-wide slots for pods and a 4-in.-wide slot for spoons.

Install the butcher block and drawer

On the left side of the coffee organizer, install the butcher block (L) and drawer using your drawer slides and the included hardware. Both attach to the left side (C) and center divider (D), so install the butcher block first and the drawer above it. Pre-drill and hand-screw for proper alignment and to avoid stripping the screws.

Once the butcher block (L) and drawer are installed, cover the left compartment with the top (A), securing it with glue and 18-gauge brad nails. The right side stays open.

Then attach the drawer front (K) to the drawer box front so it overlaps the left side (C) and center divider (D). Use double-sided tape to position it and 1-in. screws from inside the drawer box to lock it down.

Install dividers on the right side of the unit

Install and secure dividers on the right side of the unit with 1-1/4-inch 18-gauge brad nails and wood glue. Working from the front to the back of the coffee station:

  • Attach the front face (M) so it overlaps the front edges of the center divider (D) and right side (C), flush with the bottom of the base (B).
  • Secure the short divider (N) 6-1/4-in. back from the front face (M) and square, nailing it through the right side (C) and base (B). Toenail it to the center divider (D), or pull out the drawer and butcher block to nail through it.
  • Install the first tall divider (P) 4-in. behind the short divider, gluing and nailing it the same way. This should leave 6-3/4-in. between this divider (P) and the back (E).
  • Center the last tall divider (P) in the 6-3/4-in. opening between the other divider (P) and the back (E), so the back two compartments are about 3-1/16-in. deep.
  • Add the lid (Q) over the last compartment, using a 10-in. chunk of piano hinge to secure it to the back (E). Cut the piano hinge to length with a hacksaw. Just be strategic about cutting between the links, and file the cut end to make the sharp edge safe for handling.

Divide the front compartment

In the 6-1/4-in. space between the front face (M) and the short divider (N), install the tea separators (R) and spacers (S and T) to make a divided area for sugar, teas, stirrers, etc. Use a 23-gauge nailer and 5/8-in. nails to secure the spacers (S and T) to the front face (M) and short divider (N), then slide the tea separators (R) into the gaps between them. My compartments were 2-1/8-in. and 3-in. wide, but feel free to make them whatever size you’d like.

Finishing touches

Sink any protruding nails, fill the nail holes with wood filler, and finish-sand the entire piece. Apply a finish to the whole unit. I used Tried & True Original Wood Finish, which is food-safe, so it works on the butcher block and everything else

Then install the handles on the drawer and butcher block. You can’t reach behind the solid butcher block to drive a screw, so cut the head off the handle screw with a hacksaw, drill a pilot hole, and glue the cut end into it with CA glue or epoxy.

FAQ

What makes a wood finish food-safe?

A food-safe wood finish won’t transfer chemicals or toxins to the food when being used. There are two ways a finish is considered food-safe. Either it is completely non-toxic and edible in its liquid state from its origin, or, once fully cured, the VOCs (volatile organic compounds) in the finish disperse, and it becomes a stable, inert, non-toxic solid. Finishes like food-grade mineral oil or fractionated coconut oil are considered food-safe from the time of application and work well as food-safe wood finishes.

What should be included in a coffee station?

A coffee station should include options for coffee or tea, sweeteners, flavoring and stirring. Focus on organization and easy access tiers – no matter what you choose to present in your coffee station.

What is the best height for a coffee station cabinet?

42-in. works well for a free-standing coffee station cabinet. This is slightly higher than a standard 36-in. countertop height and lower than a 45-in. bar height top. For a coffee station on a countertop beneath upper cabinets, you want enough clearance to open and close your coffee maker’s lid. A 6-in. tall coffee station would give you 12-in. clearance in a standard 18-in. opening between the top of the counter and the bottom of the upper cabinets.

The post This DIY Coffee Station Can Be Built Using Only Scrap Wood appeared first on Family Handyman.

issues.title: Has That Final Destination Truck Scene Ever Actually Happened in Real Life?
issues.summary: Here's what real-world crash data actually says about the likelihood of a Final Destination truck scene. The post Has That Final Destination Truck Scene Ever Actually Happened in Real Life? appeared first on Family Handyman .
issues.author: Harrison Kral
issues.content_html:
Giving drivers a reason to fear logging trucks since 2003, Final Destination 2 opened with one of the franchise’s most visceral—and memorable—scenes. A logging truck traveling down a busy highway spills its cargo and sets off a chain reaction of intense car crashes. It’s a gruesome, cinematic disaster, but the basic danger is grounded in reality. Logs can come loose during transport, with serious consequences on a busy road. H as anything like the Final Destination truck scene actually happened in real life?

Has the Final Destination Truck Scene Ever Happened in Real Life?

Yes, there have been real-life incidents where logging trucks lost their cargo and caused major highway accidents. However, the Final Destination truck scene depicting this realistic road hazard is grossly exaggerated. Logs can fall off of trucks and cause accidents, but they don’t bounce down the highway and become windshield-level projectiles like in the film. So, yes, the danger is real, but the chain-reaction chaos depicted in the film is highly dramatized.

Real-Life Accidents Involving Cargo Falling Off Trucks

In January 2024, a logging truck on Interstate 95 in Florida overturned while traveling too fast through a curve in the road. Logs spilled onto the highway, rolled over a barrier and into oncoming traffic. A Jacksonville man who was involved in the accident told local reporters, “I just had a real life Final Destination moment…” However, he and all other motorists were unharmed. In June of 2025, another turnover dumped not logs, but large metal pipes across Highway 75 in Tulsa, Oklahoma, closing both lanes of traffic. Again, no injuries were reported. A fatal accident involving a logging truck did occur in Arkansas in 2014. While traveling down Highway 65, the truck blew a rear tire, swerved into a bridge construction site and tipped over. Two construction workers were killed by the discharged logs.

How Common Are Accidents Caused by Unsecured Loads?

Each year, shifting or unsecured loads carried by commercial vehicles are linked to roughly 4,000 to 7,000 accidents. This may not sound like a lot, but these accidents have severe consequences, often resulting in serious injury or death. “ They regularly make news headlines, so the average person may think they’re more common than they are,” personal injury attorney Juan Dominguez says. In fact, the most dangerous vehicles carrying cargo are non-commercial cars and trucks . 73 percent of highway accidents involving road debris are caused by passenger vehicles with unsecured loads . Commercial trucks are closely regulated and inspected for proper load security, contributing to lower accident rates. Despite the attention given to logging truck accidents, they are only involved in 1.5 percent of all fatal commercial truck accidents each year.

How To Stay Safe Around Trucks Carrying Large Loads

Take control of your safety when sharing the road with large cargo trucks. Here’s how:

Increase your following distance

“ My first rule is to never drive directly behind a truck with a [loose] load like logs, pipes or steel beams,” construction safety specialist Steven Menotti says. “If the load shifts or falls off, you’ll be the first vehicle it hits.” If you have to drive behind a cargo truck, increase your following distance to at least four seconds, which allows for more reaction time if debris falls into the road. “ That distance can help if the unexpected happens and something comes loose,” Dominguez says. “You have more time to try and react.” If possible, reduce your speed for a shorter stopping distance.

Pass quickly

If you need to pass a truck on the highway, time it so you can quickly complete the pass and return to the lane. Avoid driving directly next to a cargo truck for an extended length of time to avoid being hit by falling debris or cargo.

Know the danger signs

If you spot a truck without a properly secured load, move away from it on the road. Look for worn or loose straps and chains, unevenly loaded cargo or missing side stakes. “Those all indicate the trucker probably didn’t check the load,” Menotti says. “I won’t follow it. I change lanes, and pull far back.”

FAQ

How Realistic Is the Log Truck Scene in Final Destination 2?

Logs can fall from trucks, but they don’t bounce or become projectiles across the highway like the Final Destination truck scene. In the film, this depiction was CGI-generated.

What Should You Do if Cargo Falls Off a Truck in Front of You?

Brake hard and avoid swerving. Swerving causes 37 percent of all road debris accident fatalities, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA).

ABOUT THE EXPERTS

  • Steven Menotti is CEO at Menotti Enterprise , a safety consulting company for construction firms based in New York City.
  • Juan Dominguez is the founder, CEO and managing partner at The Dominguez Firm , LLP, a personal injury firm in Los Angeles.

issues.title: Waymo Is Banned From California Freeways, For Now — Here’s Why
issues.summary: California banned Waymo from freeways after a series of safety incidents. Here's why regulators stepped in and what it means for riders. The post Waymo Is Banned From California Freeways, For Now — Here’s Why appeared first on Family Handyman .
issues.author: Alex Shoemaker
issues.content_html:
Driving through a construction zone can be confusing, especially when lanes are closed or police are directing traffic. Waymo’s self-driving cars have run into problems in these situations, too.

On Nov. 11, California banned Waymo from operating driverless vehicles on freeways following several incidents involving road crews and police. The company has since stopped freeway rides in other states as well.

Here’s why California stepped in and what the ban means for Waymo passengers.

Why California Banned Waymo From Freeways After Multiple Safety Incidents

The California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) said the incidents put construction workers and other drivers at risk.

On Nov. 5, three Waymo vehicles entered an active construction zone on Highway 101 near Burlingame, where crews were working. Waymo said no one was injured, and no collisions occurred.

The next day, another Waymo attempted to pass California Highway Patrol vehicles during a traffic break on Interstate 280. Officers use traffic breaks to slow or stop vehicles, often because of roadwork or a hazard ahead. Drivers must stay behind the patrol cars until officers allow traffic to resume.

Waymo had similar problems in May, which led to a temporary suspension and software changes. But new incidents occurred in November.

In April, California approved stricter rules for self-driving cars. DMV Director Steve Gordon said the changes would bring “additional accountability for AV manufacturers.”

The freeway ban doesn’t affect Waymo’s regular street service, although some trips may take longer. Waymo has also voluntarily stopped commercial freeway rides in other states while it looks into what went wrong.

Why Waymo Struggles With Freeway Construction Zones and When the Ban Could End

Waymo’s cars use cameras and sensors to monitor traffic, but construction zones don’t always follow normal traffic patterns. The recent incidents showed problems with how the vehicles responded to road closures and police activity.

There’s no date yet for Waymo to return to California freeways. The DMV wants the company to show that its cars can safely handle road closures and police activity before allowing driverless freeway rides again.

Waymo says it’s working with state officials and will continue testing on freeways with trained specialists behind the wheel. Passengers can still book rides on regular streets in the meantime.

issues.title: GLP-1s Like Ozempic May Boost Brain Health, But Can They Lower Dementia Risk?
issues.summary: Research suggests that GLP-1 medications may positively affect brain health. Ekaterina Demidova · Moment/Getty A review in Science suggests glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) medications may be linked to better brain health. It’s still unclear whether they act directly on the brain or whether benefits stem from improved cardiometabolic health. Observational studies suggest GLP-1 medications may be as
issues.content_html:
• A review in Science suggests glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) medications may be linked to better brain health.
  • It’s still unclear whether they act directly on the brain or whether benefits stem from improved cardiometabolic health.
  • Observational studies suggest GLP-1 medications may be associated with a lower risk of cognitive impairment and dementia in people with obesity or type 2 diabetes. However, a direct causal relationship hasn’t been proven.
  • Semaglutide didn’t slow progression in two phase 3 trials of early Alzheimer’s disease.

GLP-1 medications have transformed obesity and type 2 diabetes treatment. Now, researchers are investigating whether the effects of this blockbuster class of drugs extend beyond weight loss and affect brain health.

A comprehensive new review published on November 5 in the journal Science evaluated the current evidence on how GLP-1 medications like semaglutide and tirzepatide may affect the brain across aging, cardiometabolic disease, and Alzheimer’s disease.

The authors of the review suggested that GLP-1 medications like Ozempic and Zepbound may offer brain health benefits. However, they were also left with the question of whether the medications act directly on the brain or whether better brain health is actually a consequence of improved cardiometabolic health.

Sheena Aurora, MD, vice president, Medical Affairs, Alzheimer’s Association, who wasn’t involved in the review, told Healthline that more research is needed to better understand the effects of GLP-1 drugs on the brain.

“While research suggests GLP-1s could reduce brain inflammation, improve blood vessel health, and even protect neurons, much broader, randomized clinical trials on GLP-1s and brain health, including in people with Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias, are needed,” she said.

GLP-1s may lower cognitive decline risk in obesity, diabetes

GLP-1 medications like semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, mimic the GLP-1 hormone. Tirzepatide, the active ingredient in Mounjaro and Zepbound, also targets a second hormone pathway called GIP.

These medications have been shown to produce significant weight loss and improvements in cardiometabolic health.

This is important for brain health because obesity,type 2 diabetes, and vascular dysfunction are all linked with cognitive impairment and dementia. Insulin resistance and chronic inflammation may also link metabolic and brain health.

Analyses of large outcome trials and observational cohorts have suggested that GLP-1 medications may be associated with a reduced risk of cognitive impairment and dementia. However, randomized trials in diseases like Alzheimer’s disease have yet to demonstrate clinical benefits.

Around 200 preclinical and mechanistic studies have shown benefits for learning, memory, synaptic plasticity, and neuronal resilience, though results are heterogeneous in design and direction, so a clear consensus on magnitude and mechanism remains lacking.

It is also unclear how well GLP-1 medications reach the brain. They appear to reach certain areas, such as the hypothalamus, brainstem, and circumventricular organs, more readily than regions protected by the blood-brain barrier.

The report authors noted that some studies have shown that GLP-1 receptor agonists may reduce the risk of cognitive impairment and dementia in people with type 2 diabetes. This may be due to cognitive issues being linked to factors such as blood sugar, blood pressure, vascular health, and sleep.

Mir Ali, MD, medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline, “These findings are interesting, but like many of the other benefits associated with GLP-1 medications, a direct causal relationship has not yet been proven.”

“Rather, the benefits appear to be more closely tied to the reduction in obesity and better control of diabetes,” he said.

Your heart health may affect your brain health

Aurora noted that growing evidence supports the heart-brain connection.

She cited new findings from the Alzheimer’s Association’s landmark U.S. POINTER study presented at the Clinical Trials in Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) conference November 16–19 in Boston, MA.

The research showed that the structured lifestyle intervention program also improved heart health risk factors, such as:

  • body mass index (BMI)
  • waist circumference
  • blood sugar
  • blood pressure
  • resting heart rate
  • cholesterol

“U.S. POINTER can change those risk factors within 24 months, and better heart health risk-factor control was linked with better cognition,” Aurora said. “We’re also interested to see whether adding a drug like a GLP-1 to a U.S. POINTER-style lifestyle program improves cognition in at-risk older adults more than the program alone.”

To find out, the Alzheimer’s Association is funding the Prevention of Risk for Cognitive Decline through Combined Therapy (PROTECT-Cog) global phase 3 clinical trial.

PROTECT-Cog is a first-of-its-kind trial designed to evaluate whether combining a proven multidomain lifestyle intervention with a metabolism-targeting drug, like a GLP-1, can further reduce the risk of cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment, and dementia in at-risk older adults.

Dung Trinh, MD, internist at MemorialCare Medical Group and Chief Medical Officer of Healthy Brain Clinic in Irvine, CA, who also wasn’t involved in the review, told Healthline, “I often remind my patients that what’s good for the heart is generally good for the brain.”

“The brain depends on a healthy cardiovascular system to deliver a constant supply of oxygen, glucose, and other nutrients. Conditions such as high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, and high cholesterol can damage blood vessels, promote chronic inflammation, and increase the risk of stroke and vascular cognitive impairment,” he said.

“Over time, these changes can also contribute to the development or progression of dementia.”

Trinh added that while GLP-1 medications can improve several cardiometabolic risk factors, these improvements do not automatically translate into proven dementia prevention.

“Regular physical activity, a heart-healthy diet, adequate sleep, and management of cardiovascular risk factors remain essential strategies for maintaining brain health as we age,” he said.

Can GLP-1s help with Alzheimer’s disease?

When the report authors turned their attention to more stringent tests on semaglutide in people already living with early Alzheimer’s disease, the picture began to change.

Novo Nordisk’s EVOKE and EVOKE + Phase 3 Trials examined the efficacy of semaglutide in people with early stage Alzheimer’s disease.

The studies showed that while semaglutide produced changes in several disease-related biomarkers, it didn’t slow the progression of Alzheimer’s disease.

This emphasizes that fixing metabolic issues might prevent cognitive decline in someone with obesity or diabetes. But it might not be enough to reverse the damage in someone with established Alzheimer’s disease, where profound synaptic loss and protein pathology have already occurred.

The review authors suggest that future research on obesity and diabetes should also include rigorous and specific cognitive testing.

issues.title: ‘Root-to-Tip’ Eating: Are You Missing Out on Fiber by Discarding Scraps?
issues.summary: Eating typically discarded parts of fruits and vegetables could help boost your fiber intake. fcafotodigital · E+/Getty Peels, skins, seeds, and stalks of many fruits and vegetables contain significantly more fiber than the parts typically eaten — in some cases up to five times more, according to a study analyzing 12 produce types. Fiber helps regulate blood sugar, supports beneficial gut bacteria
issues.content_html:
• Peels, skins, seeds, and stalks of many fruits and vegetables contain significantly more fiber than the parts typically eaten — in some cases up to five times more, according to a study analyzing 12 produce types.
  • Fiber helps regulate blood sugar, supports beneficial gut bacteria, and may help lower LDL cholesterol, yet around 95% of adults in the United States don’t meet the recommended 25 to 30 grams daily.
  • To try root-to-tip eating safely, start small by keeping skins on apples and kiwi, slicing broccoli stalks for stir-fries, or saving vegetable trimmings for homemade broth. Always wash produce thoroughly and research new plant parts before eating them.

Eating fruit and veggie scraps may boost fiber intake and cut food waste.

This study from King’s College London found that peels, skins, seeds, and stalks of fruits and vegetables—parts often discarded—contained significantly more dietary fiber than the commonly eaten portions in 10 of 12 produce types analyzed.

In some cases, the fiber content was up to five times higher in these “root-to-tip” components.

These findings, recently published in the International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition, are noteworthy, since around 95% of U.S. adults aren’t getting enough fiber. What’s more, around one-fifth of all food produced globally is wasted every year.

Discarded parts may contain up to 5 times more fiber

The researchers identified 12 fresh produce items that were deemed suitable for “root-to-tip” inclusion:

  • beetroot
  • bell pepper
  • broccoli
  • butternut squash
  • cauliflower
  • celeriac (celery root)
  • curly kale
  • fennel
  • kiwi
  • leek
  • pineapple
  • watermelon

In the laboratory analysis, they measured the dietary fiber content of both the “root-to-tip” components (skins, peels, seeds, stalks) and the parts that people typically eat.

The key findings of the study showed that in 10 of the 12 produce types, the “root-to-tip” components contained more fiber than the parts typically consumed.

For example:

  • Watermelon rind contained 2.10 grams of fiber per 100 grams compared with around 0.6 grams in a typical serving.
  • Butternut squash skins and seeds contained 9.25 grams of fiber per 100 grams compared with 2 grams in the flesh.
  • Pineapple skin and core contained five times more fiber (453.7%) than the flesh.

However, broccoli stalks contained 28.4% less fiber than the florets that people usually eat, meaning individuals are already consuming the most fiber-rich part.

Most participants in focus groups saw the nutritional value of the “root-to-tip” approach as more of a motivator than its sustainability.

However, these findings show that a “root-to-tip” approach to many fruits and vegetables could not only support higher dietary fiber intake but also reduce food waste.

Kristin Kirkpatrick, president of KAK, Consulting, LLC, and a dietitian at the Cleveland Clinic Department of Wellness & Preventive Medicine, said that the takeaway isn’t to eat every peel or seed, but to look for safe, simple ways to get more fiber from the foods you’re already buying. Kirkpatrick wasn’t involved in the study.

This applies to some of the plants analyzed in this study, but not all produce. For instance, you can only eat a kiwi that’s peeled. This is still a better choice than no kiwi (or a processed-food snack in its place) at all.

Why fiber matters for long-term health

Fiber is important for promoting health and preventing chronic conditions such as cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, colorectal cancer, and obesity.

“Fiber does much more than support regular bowel movements. It helps regulate blood sugar, supports beneficial gut bacteria, and certain types of soluble fiber can help lower LDL cholesterol by increasing bile acid elimination,” noted Michelle Routhenstein, a preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished, who wasn’t involved in the study.

On average, adults are recommended to get 25–30 grams (or more, depending on age) of fiber daily.

Both nutrition experts told Healthline that people generally aren’t getting enough fiber because of their food options or choices.

“Most likely because individuals are not consuming enough plants, and overconsuming processed and ultra-processed foods which are typically very low in fiber,” said Kirkpatrick. “Simply not eating enough fruits and vegetables or choosing white refined grains over whole grains can be why a person’s diet is lacking fiber.”

Routhenstein added, “I think it is important that when we talk about fiber we point out that it doesn’t have to mean completely changing how you eat. I encourage people to incorporate fiber-rich ingredients into familiar, culturally meaningful foods they already enjoy.”

“Start with small increases with foods you enjoy and build gradually to allow your digestive system to adjust.”

How to safely try ‘root-to-tip’ eating at home

It is important to always research any new plant parts before eating them, wash thoroughly, and consult a healthcare professional if you have digestive conditions or concerns.

And remember that not all produce scraps are edible or recommended.

“Any dietary change will be dependent on personal preference. Some individuals may not enjoy or may not know how to add components of a plant they are not used to,” said Kirkpatrick.

She noted that, based on the study’s examples, an easier option might be to add more kiwi peels and seeds. “In fact, kiwi skin is probably the most practical fruit peel to highlight for consumers,” she said.

Routhenstein added, “I think there is a knowledge gap that the skins, peels, from the root to the tip are edible and nutritious, so we need to start there.”

She suggested that one way to start is by eating the skins of apples, pears, and well-scrubbed carrots. Trim and thinly slice broccoli stalks for stir-fries or soups. Sautée beet greens and stems just as you would spinach. Freeze appropriate vegetable trimmings, such as carrot ends and celery leaves, for homemade broth.

“Root-to-tip eating helps reduce food waste by encouraging us to use more of the edible portions of fruits and vegetables rather than discarding them. It also maximizes the nutritional and economic value of the food we purchase while making better use of the water, land, and energy required to produce it,” said Routhenstein.

“The key is finding simple, enjoyable ways to incorporate these parts into meals we already eat.”

issues.title: Are Ultra-Processed Foods Raising Your Risk of Stroke and Obesity?
issues.summary: Research shows that a high intake of UPFs can increase your risk of stroke, obesity, and various other conditions. katerinasergeevna · E+/Getty Recent studies suggest that higher intake of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) may be linked to increased risks of stroke, heart disease, cancer, obesity, diabetes, and cognitive decline. Research indicates that fructose in UPFs is processed differently from ot
issues.content_html:
• Recent studies suggest that higher intake of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) may be linked to increased risks of stroke, heart disease, cancer, obesity, diabetes, and cognitive decline.
  • Research indicates that fructose in UPFs is processed differently from other sugars — it bypasses normal energy pathways and may contribute to liver fat buildup and metabolic syndrome.
  • You can reduce health risks by lowering UPF intake through simple food swaps, like choosing whole grains, lean proteins, and brightly colored fruits and vegetables over processed options.

High intakes of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) have been linked to multiple adverse health outcomes, including an increased risk of stroke, heart disease, cancer, and obesity.

A recent study published in JAMA Open Network showed that a higher intake of UPFs may be linked to brain damage and could lead to an increased risk of stroke and cognitive decline later in life.

Another large study in Family Medicine and Community Health found that people who consumed the most UPFs were at a higher risk of developing chronic diseases, such as diabetes, obesity, heart disease, and cancer.

An earlier review in Nature Metabolism also showed that fructose in UPFs may contribute to obesity and metabolic diseases.

Together, these studies add to research on the effects of eating high levels of UPFs on your health.

Ultra-processed foods linked to stroke risk

A recent study published in JAMA Network Open found that healthy adults who eat higher levels of UPFs may be more likely to experience damage to their brain that could increase the risk of stroke and future memory problems.

The cross-sectional study analyzed 8,783 adults between the ages of 35 and 69 without cardiovascular disease. The researchers used MRI scans to evaluate participants’ brains and measured UPF intake using a food frequency questionnaire.

UPFs accounted for an average of 25% of participants’ diet. However, among those with the highest intake, these foods accounted for 45% of their daily intake, compared with 16% among those with the lowest intake.

When comparing the highest intake to the lowest, the researchers found that those in the higher group had 1.7% more body fat and had a higher risk of vascular brain injury (VBI).

The findings suggest that there may be a link between high UPF intake and brain changes that could increase the risk of stroke and cognitive decline.

“These findings are concerning, but it is important to remember that an association does not prove cause and effect,” Michelle Routhenstein, a preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline in a previous interview.

“While we can’t conclude from this study that limiting UPFs would improve brain health, we have decades of literature demonstrating that higher intakes of green leafy vegetables, brightly colored fruits, whole grains, and lean protein sources are good for brain health,” Suzanne Judd, PhD, director of the UC College of Medicine’s Center for Public Health, who wasn’t involved in the study, previously told Healthline.

Routhenstein advised starting simply with one manageable swap to help lower your UPF intake.

“I want people to feel empowered, not fearful, when making food choices,” she said. “Healthy eating does not mean having to cook everything from scratch. What matters most is building consistent, nourishing habits that support both heart and brain health.”

Key points

  • Healthy adults who consume high amounts of UPFs may be more likely to show signs of vascular brain injury, which has been linked to stroke risk and cognitive decline.
  • People with the highest UPF intake had higher body fat levels and greater odds of vascular brain injury than those with the lowest intake.
  • You can reduce UPF intake by making simple swaps.

UPF consumption may raise risk of multiple diseases

A large recent study published in Family Medicine and Community Health found that people who ate the most UPFs were more likely to develop chronic diseases, such as:

  • heart disease
  • cancer
  • obesity
  • metabolic syndrome
  • diabetes
  • mental health conditions
  • digestive diseases

It also found that these individuals may have a higher overall risk of death.

The research team analyzed 51 studies involving nearly 9 million participants from around the world, with follow-up periods ranging from 2 to 32 years.

They found that consuming high levels of UPFs was associated with an increased risk of many chronic health issues.

Those with the highest levels of UPF consumption showed a:

  • 24% higher risk of cardiovascular events like heart attacks and strokes
  • 23% higher risk of obesity or overweight
  • 24% higher risk of metabolic syndrome or diabetes
  • 27% higher risk of depression and anxiety
  • 31% higher risk of digestive diseases, including Crohn’s disease
  • 12% higher risk of cancer
  • 18% higher risk of death from any cause

These numbers were derived by comparing people who ate the most UPFs with those who ate the least.

Johannah Katz, MA, a registered dietitian at Nourish, who was not involved in the study, told Healthline in a previous interview that there isn’t currently a cutoff point at which ultra-processed foods become harmful.

“What this new research suggests is more of a dose-response relationship; the more ultra-processed food in the diet, the higher the observed risk for several chronic diseases,” she said.

Reducing UPF intake may help decrease these risks.

Key points

  • Eating more ultra-processed foods (UPFs) may be linked to a higher risk of disease and early death.
  • The risk of chronic diseases increases with higher UPF consumption.
  • Reducing UPF intake may help decrease the risk.

Fructose in UPFs linked to higher risk of obesity

A recent review published in Nature Metabolism highlighted the role fructose can play in driving disease, distinct from its role as a source of calories.

Fructose is a simple sugar that is found both naturally, in fruits and honey, and in sweeteners like high fructose corn syrup and sucrose (table sugar).

One reason that fructose can be problematic is that it has twice the sweetness of glucose, which can lead to increased cravings for more fructose-containing foods and drinks.

“Fructose found in these processed forms is not handled the same way as regular blood sugar,” Routhestein, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline in aprevious interview. “When it is consumed, it goes to the liver, where it easily turns into fat, which can build up in the liver and around the organs and contribute to conditions like fatty liver and metabolic syndrome.”

This recent review highlights how fructose metabolism bypasses key steps in energy-processing pathways. This can lead to various effects, such as:

  • increased fat synthesis
  • depletion of cellular energy
  • production of compounds associated with metabolic syndrome

“The emerging body of research suggests that fructose is not metabolically identical to all other carbohydrates, especially when it is consumed in excess through sugar-sweetened beverages and ultra-processed foods,” Serena Poon, certified nutritionist & longevity wellness advisor, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline in a previous interview.

“Excess calories still matter, but fructose may affect metabolism differently than other sugars, particularly in the liver … In my view, this supports a more nuanced conversation because it is not just about sugar in the abstract, but also about the form, dose, and dietary context in which fructose is consumed,” she said.

Key points

  • A recent review found that fructose plays a role in driving disease.
  • The research showed that fructose’s effects on the body may be associated with metabolic syndrome.
  • Understanding the effects of fructose on the body may help develop new strategies to prevent and treat metabolic diseases.
